content.user_title: Set Up Firebase Crashlytics for Mobile Apps
content.value_statement: Mobile teams need reliable crash reports before release issues reach users. This skill guides Android and iOS Crashlytics setup, test crashes, and report verification.
actual_capabilities: Guides Android Crashlytics setup with Gradle plugins, Firebase BoM, and SDK dependencies.
Guides iOS Crashlytics setup with Swift Package Manager and dSYM upload verification.
Explains required Firebase project, app, and configuration file prerequisites.
Shows how to force a test crash and verify the report in Firebase.
Points users to official Firebase guidance for custom keys, logs, and user identifiers.
limitations: It does not create Firebase projects without Firebase CLI access and user approval.
It depends on Firebase console permissions or MCP credentials for report verification.
It references other setup skills for Firebase basics and Xcode project changes.
It does not guarantee current SDK versions without checking official repositories.

use_cases.title: Add Android Crash Reporting
use_cases.description: Set up Crashlytics dependencies, Gradle plugins, app configuration, and a test crash workflow for a Kotlin or Java Android app.

use_cases.title: Configure iOS Symbolication
use_cases.description: Add FirebaseCrashlytics through Swift Package Manager and verify the dSYM upload script for readable crash reports.

use_cases.title: Standardize Release Verification
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable Crashlytics setup and validation checklist for multiple mobile apps before production release.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Android Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up Crashlytics for my Android app. Check the prerequisites, tell me which Gradle files change, and explain how to verify a test crash.

prompt_templates.title: Guide iOS Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through Firebase Crashlytics setup for an iOS app that already has Firebase Core. Include dSYM upload verification and test crash steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Existing Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my existing Crashlytics setup for Android and iOS. Identify missing config files, dependency gaps, verification steps, and cleanup tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multi-App Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a rollout plan for Crashlytics across several mobile apps. Include Firebase project mapping, CLI confirmation points, privacy checks, and verification criteria.

output_examples.input: I need Crashlytics in a Kotlin Android app.
output: Checks for a Firebase project, Android app registration, and google-services.json before Gradle changes.
Explains the project plugin, app plugin, Firebase BoM, and Crashlytics dependency.
Provides a test crash workflow and reminds the user to remove the trigger.

output_examples.input: Help me verify Crashlytics on iOS.
output: Confirms Firebase initialization, package installation, and dSYM upload settings.
Explains why the debugger should be disconnected for simulator crash testing.
Lists Firebase console and MCP verification paths.

output_examples.input: Review our mobile crash reporting readiness.
output: Summarizes Android and iOS configuration gaps.
Identifies test crash, symbolication, privacy, and cleanup checks.
Creates a short release verification checklist.

best_practices: Confirm Firebase project IDs, app IDs, and configuration files before changing project files.
Pin CLI and SDK versions when setup commands are used in repeatable automation.
Remove forced crash code immediately after Firebase receives the validation report.
anti_patterns: Running unpinned npx commands automatically in production setup workflows.
Leaving forced test crashes in application startup code after verification.
Adding user identifiers or verbose logs without a privacy review.

faq.question: Does this skill install Firebase automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can guide Firebase CLI commands, but installation and project changes require user approval.

faq.question: Can it support both Android and iOS apps?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes separate setup references for Android Gradle projects and iOS Swift Package projects.

faq.question: Does it read my crash reports?
faq.answer: Only when the environment has Firebase MCP access and valid credentials. Otherwise, it explains Firebase console verification.

faq.question: Will it choose current SDK versions?
faq.answer: It directs users to official Firebase repositories for current versions. Verify versions before editing project files.

faq.question: Is test crash code safe to keep?
faq.answer: No. Remove the forced crash trigger after Crashlytics receives the validation report.

faq.question: Can Crashlytics data include personal information?
faq.answer: Yes. Review custom keys, logs, and user identifiers before collecting them in crash reports.
